entry.title: Kraken parent Payward explores becoming full bank outside US
entry.summary: Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, is exploring becoming a full bank outside the US, expanding into banking, lending, and asset management, with mortgages a future possibility. This move signals further institutionalization of the crypto industry as major players push into traditional financial services. It could also set a precedent for other crypto firms seeking banking licenses abroad, blurring the line between crypto and conventional banking. The exploration is at a strategic stage, with no regulatory finality or immediate market impact. The bank would operate outside the US, though specific jurisdictions have not been disclosed.

entry.title: Binance launches Agent OS, opening crypto trading to AI agents with user-set controls
entry.summary: Binance has launched Agent OS, a developer platform that lets AI agents access market data, monitor accounts, and execute crypto trades on the exchange. The platform supports AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, with user-configured permissions and limits. This marks a major step by a leading exchange toward autonomous AI-driven trading, potentially reshaping how crypto trades are executed and managed. It also accelerates the broader trend of AI agents participating in onchain and financial infrastructure, affecting traders, developers, and the AI-crypto ecosystem. Users can assign agents to dedicated subaccounts to isolate funds and activity, set permissions, and revoke access at any time. Binance can monitor trades placed through Agent OS but cannot see an agent's external data sources or decision-making, and the service is not available to users in the EEA.

entry.title: LayerZero loses a dozen partners as ZRO drops 31% in 2025
entry.summary: LayerZero has lost a dozen partnerships this year, including Nethermind, Kelp DAO, Kraken, and BitGo, as its ZRO token fell by a third. The latest departure, Nethermind, terminated its role as a verifier on Wednesday and migrated to a competitor. This exodus signals declining trust in LayerZero's security model after the Lazarus Group incident, with billions in bridged assets moving off the protocol. As a leading interoperability platform, losing major enterprise and institutional users erodes network effects and could reshape the cross-chain bridge landscape. By early July, more than $7 billion in assets had already migrated off LayerZero, and BitGo's exit pushed the cumulative total toward $15 billion. In July, LayerZero announced it was winding down support for low-activity chains and set an August 3 deadline for teams still using v1 libraries.

entry.title: Optimism moves 546.9M OP from airdrops to ecosystem growth fund
entry.summary: Optimism's governance has approved a proposal to repurpose 546.9 million OP tokens previously reserved for user airdrops into a new Strategic Ecosystem Fund. The fund will back partnerships, incentives, and institutional adoption including OP Enterprise. This decision materially changes OP's token distribution and signals a shift from airdrop-driven user acquisition toward institutional and enterprise growth. It reshapes user expectations and may influence incentives across the OP Superchain ecosystem. Optimism said no additional airdrops are planned after distributing 269.1 million OP across five previous rounds. At current prices, the reallocated 546.9 million OP is worth about $50 million, close to a quarter of OP's roughly $211 million market cap.

entry.title: GnosisDAO Approves Gnosis Chain Transition to Ethereum Economic Zone Rollup
entry.summary: GnosisDAO approved GIP-153, passing with 123,158 GNO in favor, to transition Gnosis Chain from a standalone layer-1 into a ZK-proven Ethereum Economic Zone (EEZ) rollup that settles directly on Ethereum. The tentative launch window is late 2026 or early 2027, pending readiness of EEZ technology. This decision makes Gnosis Chain the first production EEZ instance, a significant step toward unifying Ethereum's fragmented L2 ecosystem by enabling synchronous composability across rollups without relying on bridges. It also changes Gnosis Chain's security and settlement model, shifting from its own validator set to Ethereum's validators. The proposal GIP-153 passed with 123,158 GNO in support, 115 against, and 151 abstentions across 54 voters, with turnout of 123,425 GNO exceeding the 75,000 quorum. Gnosis Chain will retire its validator set, retain xDAI as its gas token, and launch as the first deployed EEZ instance while keeping existing applications and balances.

entry.title: Arbitrum Activates Elara Upgrade With Optional Compliance Filters
entry.summary: The Arbitrum platform activated the ArbOS 61 Elara upgrade, bringing optional compliance filtering, customizable priority fees, and an alternative data API to dedicated Arbitrum chains, while delivering a more efficient base fee mechanism on Arbitrum One. Chain owners—not the ArbitrumDAO—control compliance screening on dedicated networks, and priority fees remain disabled on Arbitrum One pending a further governance vote. This upgrade introduces protocol-level compliance tooling for Layer 2/3 chains without imposing screening on Arbitrum One, preserving DAO control and user neutrality. It could make the Arbitrum stack more attractive to institutions and regulated entities that need on-chain transaction filtering for dedicated chains. ArbOS 61 Elara also quadruples Stylus contract size limits, expanding smart-contract capacity on Arbitrum chains. Compliance filtering operates across two layers—the Sequencer and the State Transition Function (STF)—ensuring restricted activity is blocked regardless of how a transaction enters the system, and it remains off by default on Arbitrum One and Nova.

entry.title: Binance to Delist ICX, SCRT, and STORJ in September 2026
entry.summary: Binance announced it will delist and cease trading for all spot trading pairs of ICON (ICX), Secret (SCRT), and Storj (STORJ) on September 3, 2026 at 03:00 UTC. The exchange cited its latest reviews for the decision. Binance is the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, so delisting removes a major source of liquidity and trading access for these tokens. This could heighten selling pressure and make it harder for holders to trade or exit positions, and it may also signal compliance or project-health concerns. The delisting applies to all spot trading pairs for the three tokens and takes effect on 2026-09-03. Each token has been under pressure: ICX is trading around $0.016–0.017, SCRT around €0.18, and STORJ around $0.04 with relatively thin volumes.

entry.title: Tether Uses NYSE Shell Company to Buy and Stake Rival USDS
entry.summary: Tether invested $134 million in the failing biopharmaceutical firm NovaBay in March and reverse-merged it into a NYSE-listed entity renamed Stablecoin Development Corporat. The vehicle has been used to purchase and stake a large amount of USDS, the decentralized stablecoin from the Sky Protocol (formerly MakerDAO). This is a notable market-structure shift because the world's largest centralized stablecoin issuer is using a public shell company to accumulate a rival decentralized stablecoin. It could reshape stablecoin competition, raise governance and transparency questions, and give USDS public-market exposure. Stablecoin Development Corporat's share price has collapsed from roughly $2.00 to $1.00, and unusual buy support has repeatedly pushed it back above $1.00, apparently to avoid NYSE delisting under the 30-day sub-$1 rule. The company says it has taken a 'greater than a 9% stake' in USDS, and its CEO, Michael Kazley, describes the position as 'wildly bullish' on the SKY Protocol.

entry.title: Musk's X Explores Stablecoin Payments for Content Creators
entry.summary: According to a CoinDesk report dated August 20, 2026, Elon Musk's X platform is exploring the use of stablecoins to pay influencers and content providers. The effort is still in an exploratory phase and no specific stablecoin or rollout timeline has been confirmed. If realized, this could give stablecoins a massively visible real-world payments use case on one of the world's largest social platforms. It also signals that mainstream internet companies are increasingly treating crypto-based payments as a viable infrastructure for creator monetization. The report emphasizes that the exploration is preliminary and that X has not publicly announced any partnership with a stablecoin issuer. The move would build on Musk's long-standing interest in integrating payments into X, which has already obtained money-transmitter licenses in several U.S. states.
